markdown_chunks.section: **A detailed modelling on spray atomisation and** **combustion of LOX/GCH4 in variable area pintle** **injector rocket engines** > Nomenclature
markdown_chunks.text:
The schematic of the pintle injector, and their spray formation and breakups are shown
in Figure 1. Because of axisymmetric configuration, therefore, a 2D-axisymmetric model
was used in this simulation to reduce the computing time. And also, the three-dimensional
influence was presumed to be negligible the dimensions of pintle injector is provided in
Table 2. The VOF approach was employed to simulate the sheet formation and primary
breakup, while the Lagrangian approach was employed to simulate the secondary breakup.
These simulations were performed separately to reduce computational expenditure. The
spray combustion under subcritical condition was taken into account to obtain a 500 N
thrust using a fixed oxidiser to fuel ratio (O/F ratio) of 3.5. Therefore, to calculate the
mass flow boundary condition, the maximum chamber pressure and nozzle expansion ratio
were assumed to be 2.0 MPa and 40.43, respectively. The specific impulse and coefficient
of thrust were calculated using NASA computer program CEA (Chemical Equilibrium
with Applications), which was used to calculate the total mass flow rate of the propellants
for the maximum chamber pressure condition (assumed as maximum throttling condition
of 100%). For 25, 50, 75% throttling condition, the mass flow rate for GCH4 and LOX
was calculated using the fixed O/F ratio = 3.5 and is provided in Table 3 for all cases in
which Cases 1–4 were considered for the conditions of four different pintle openings at a
fixed pintle tip angle ( _θpt_ = 20°). The chamber pressure increased with the pintle opening
distance because the fuel mass flow rate was increased. Similarly, Case 5 and Case 6 were
for the condition of the pintle opening of 0.2 mm at _θpt_ = 0° and 40°.
